patches.old:
I.1. “Be long-suffering[e] and sensible,” he says, “and you will gain mastery over every wicked deed and do every work of righteousness.”

I.2. “For if you are long-suffering, the holy spirit dwelling in you will be pure, not clouded by another evil spirit. Instead, dwelling in a wide space, it will exult and rejoice with the vessel in which it dwells, and will minister to God with much cheerfulness, having vitality within itself.”

I.3. “But if a quick temper comes on, at once the holy spirit, being tender, is cramped, without a clean place, and seeks to withdraw from that place. For it is choked by the evil spirit, without room to minister to the Lord as it desires, being defiled by quick temper. For the Lord dwells in long-suffering, but the devil in quick temper.”

I.4. “So when both spirits dwell together, it is unprofitable and harmful to the person in whom they dwell.”

I.5. “For if you take a little wormwood and pour it into a jar of honey, is not all the honey spoiled? So much honey is ruined by the smallest amount of wormwood, which destroys the honey’s sweetness. It no longer has the same favor with its master, because it has become bitter and lost its usefulness. But if the wormwood is not put into the honey, the honey is found sweet and becomes useful to its master.”[e]

I.6. “You see, then, that long-suffering is sweeter than honey and useful to the Lord, and he dwells in it. But quick temper is bitter and useless. So if quick temper is mixed with long-suffering, long-suffering is defiled, and that person’s prayer is not useful to God.”[a]

I.7. “Sir,” I say, “I wanted to know how quick temper works, so that I may guard against it.” “Indeed,” he says, “if you and your household do not guard against it, you have lost all your hope. But guard against it, for I am with you. Everyone who repents with their whole heart will also keep away from it, for I will be with them and will protect them; for they have all been justified by the most revered angel.”[b][c]

II.1. “Now hear,” he says, “how quick temper works, how evil it is, how it overthrows God’s servants by its own activity, and how it leads them astray from righteousness. But it does not lead astray those who are full in faith, nor can it act upon them, because the Lord’s power is with them. It leads astray those who are empty and double-minded.”[d]

II.2. “For when it sees such people standing firm, it inserts itself into a person’s heart. Out of nothing, the man or woman becomes bitter over everyday matters: food, some petty matter, a friend, giving or receiving, or foolish matters like these. For all these things are foolish, empty, senseless and unprofitable for God’s servants.”[f]

II.3. “But long-suffering is great and strong, possessing mighty and vigorous power, flourishing in a wide space, cheerfully rejoicing, free from care, glorifying the Lord at all times. It has nothing bitter within itself, but always remains gentle and quiet. This long-suffering dwells with those whose faith is complete.”

II.4. “But quick temper is first foolish, flighty and senseless. Then from senselessness comes bitterness, from bitterness anger, from anger wrath, and from wrath rage. Then rage, composed of so many evils, becomes a great and incurable sin.”

II.5. “For when all these spirits dwell in one vessel, where the holy spirit also dwells, that vessel cannot contain them, but overflows.”

II.6. “So the tender spirit, unaccustomed to dwelling with an evil spirit or with hardness, withdraws from such a person and seeks to dwell with gentleness and quiet.”

II.7. “Then, when it departs from the person in whom it dwells, that person becomes empty of the righteous spirit. Afterward, filled with evil spirits, they are unstable in every deed, dragged here and there by the evil spirits, and are altogether blinded in their good understanding. This is what happens to all who are quick-tempered.”[g]

II.8. “So keep away from quick temper, that most wicked spirit. Clothe yourself with long-suffering, and stand against quick temper and bitterness, and you will be found with the dignity beloved by the Lord. See, then, that you never forget this command. For if you master this command, you will also be able to keep the other commands I am going to give you. Be strong in them and be empowered, and let everyone who wishes to walk in them be empowered.”[h]

patches.reason: Three bounded corrections after comparison with the supplied Greek: reconsideration of prior lexical decision εὐθηνία replaces vigor-oriented “vitality” with “abundance,” consistent with εὐθηνουμένη in II.3; ἀποτυφλοῦται ἀπὸ τῆς διανοίας τῆς ἀγαθῆς describes blindness cutting the person off from good understanding, not blindness within good understanding; reconsideration of prior lexical decision παρενθυμηθῇς replaces memory-only “forget” with “neglect.” All paragraph divisions, markers, difficult teachings and servant terminology remain unchanged.

I.1. “Be patient[e] and sensible,” he says. “You will overcome every evil deed and do everything that is right.”

I.2. “If you are patient, the holy spirit living in you will be pure. No other evil spirit will darken it. It will have plenty of room and rejoice with the vessel where it lives. It will serve God very gladly, with vitality within itself.”

I.3. “But if a quick temper comes over you, the tender holy spirit is crowded at once. It has no clean place and wants to leave. The evil spirit chokes it. Quick temper defiles it and leaves it no room to serve the Lord as it wishes. The Lord lives in patience, but the devil in quick temper.”

I.4. “When both spirits live together, it does no good and harms the person they live in.”

I.5. “Put a little wormwood into a jar of honey. Does it not spoil all the honey? Even a tiny amount ruins so much honey and destroys its sweetness. Its owner no longer values it as before, because it has become bitter and useless. But without the wormwood, the honey stays sweet and useful to its owner.”[e]

I.6. “You see that patience is sweeter than honey and useful to the Lord. He lives in it. But quick temper is bitter and useless. If quick temper mixes with patience, patience is defiled, and that person’s prayer is not useful to God.”[a]

I.7. “Sir,” I say, “I wanted to know how quick temper works so I can guard against it.” He says, “If you and your household do not guard against it, you have lost all your hope. Guard against it, because I am with you. Everyone who repents with their whole heart will keep away from it. I will be with them and protect them. They have all been justified by the most revered angel.”[b][c]

II.1. “Now hear how quick temper works,” he says. “It is evil. By its activity it overthrows God’s servants and leads them away from righteousness. But it cannot lead away or act on those who are full in faith, because the Lord’s power is with them. It leads away those who are empty and double-minded.”[d]

II.2. “When it sees people like these standing firm, it puts itself into their heart. For no reason, a man or woman becomes bitter about everyday things: food, a small matter, a friend, giving or receiving, or other foolish matters. All these things are foolish, empty, senseless and no good for God’s servants.”[f]

II.3. “Patience is great and strong. Its power is mighty and vigorous. It flourishes with plenty of room, rejoices gladly, is free from care and glorifies the Lord at all times. It has no bitterness inside. It always stays gentle and quiet. This patience lives with people whose faith is complete.”

II.4. “Quick temper is foolish, flighty and senseless. Senselessness produces bitterness. Bitterness produces anger, anger produces wrath, and wrath produces rage. Rage, made up of so many evils, becomes a great sin that cannot be cured.”

II.5. “When all these spirits live in one vessel, where the holy spirit also lives, the vessel cannot hold them. It overflows.”

II.6. “The tender spirit is not used to living with an evil spirit or with hardness. It leaves that person and looks for gentleness and quiet to live with.”

II.7. “When it leaves the person it lived in, that person is empty of the righteous spirit. Evil spirits then fill them. They are unstable in everything they do. The evil spirits pull them here and there, and they become completely blind in their good understanding. This happens to everyone with a quick temper.”[g]

II.8. “Keep away from quick temper, that most evil spirit. Put on patience. Resist quick temper and bitterness. You will be found with the dignity that the Lord loves. Never forget this command. If you master it, you can also keep the other commands I will give you. Be strong in them and be empowered. Let everyone who wants to follow them be empowered.”[h]

patches.reason: Independently compared with the supplied Greek: reconsideration of prior lexical decision εὐθηνία proposes “abundance,” rather than vigor-oriented “vitality,” retaining the internal location without specifying what the abundance consists of; “blind to good understanding” preserves the loss expressed by ἀπὸ rather than locating blindness within good understanding; reconsideration of prior lexical decision παρενθυμηθῇς proposes a warning against neglect, including βλέπε as “Be careful,” rather than a memory-only instruction. All paragraph divisions, markers, difficult teachings and servant terminology remain unchanged.

patches.old: Long-suffering is patient endurance, not merely waiting; the simplified edition uses patience. Wormwood is the bitter ingredient in the teaching comparison. The honey’s master is its owner. A wide space and vessel retain the passage’s images; vitality retains the earlier English choice for euthēnia without claiming a new lexicon consultation.

Reconsideration of the prior lexical decision: “abundance” replaces “vitality” for euthēnia. “Well-being” is an alternative; “abundance” preserves the fullness expressed by the noun without narrowing it to vigor or life-energy. The related flourishing language in II.3 supports this sense.
patches.reason: Reconciles note e with the proposed I.2 correction, explicitly compares abundance and well-being, and labels reconsideration without claiming a new consultation.
